title-proc.eng: Market dialogue, Trombaferesis machine

description-proc.eng: Oslo University Hospital HF (OUS) invites suppliers of thrombapheresis to provide input in a RFI. OUS plans to establish parallel framework agreements with up to two suppliers, for a contract period of four years, with an estimated total volume of 8 machines and a maximum total volume of 10 machines. The equipment is to be used for thrombapheresis from blood donors with simultaneous plasma collection. Enclosed are the market dialogue document with further information, and a response form containing the questions we would like answered. The market dialogue does not constitute a tender competition and entails no obligation for OUS to carry out a procurement. It is conducted as a preliminary market investigation pursuant to Section 12-1 of the Norwegian Public Procurement Regulations (forskrift om offentlige anskaffelser, FOA). Input received will be considered, but OUS remains free to design the procurement independently of it. Participation is not remunerated and confers neither an advantage nor a disadvantage in any subsequent competition.

title-proc.eng: Project "OpenJS: AI Vulnerability Disclosure"

description-proc.deu: Der Auftrag betrifft das Projekt „OpenJS: AI Vulnerability Disclosure“, das sich mit der Untersuchung befasst, wie Node.js mit Meldungen über Sicherheitslücken umgeht, da künstliche Intelligenz diese Lücken mittlerweile schneller und in größerer Zahl aufspürt. Im Rahmen von vier Arbeitspaketen umfasst der Auftrag Regeln und Werkzeuge zur Entscheidung, welche Meldungen öffentlich behandelt werden können, einen Pilotversuch, der dies an Node.js testet, einen Vergleich der Ergebnisse mit der bisherigen Bilanz des Projekts sowie veröffentlichte Leitlinien für andere Projekte. Ziel dieser Dienstleistung ist es, Sicherheitskorrekturen für Node.js schnell und zuverlässig zu gewährleisten und anderen Open-Source-Projekten einen erprobten Weg aufzuzeigen, wie sie dies ebenfalls erreichen können.
description-proc.eng: The contract concerns the project OpenJS: AI Vulnerability Disclosure, which covers research into how Node.js handles reports of security flaws now that artificial intelligence finds those flaws faster and in greater numbers. As part of four work packages, the contract covers rules and tooling for deciding which reports can be handled in public, a pilot that tests this on Node.js, a comparison of the results with the project's past record, and published guidance for other projects. The aim of this service is to keep security fixes for Node.js fast and reliable, and to give other open source projects a tested way to do the same.

title-proc.eng: HSE 29390 Extension of SAP Application Managed Service for the IFMS

description-proc.eng: Extension of the existing contract for SAP Application Managed Service for Integrated Financial Management and Procurement System (IFMS) for a period of 3 years will provide Post Go-Live SAP application support services for the IFMS SAP Solution following completion of Hypercare for the first entity to Go-Live, continuing through each deployment and onto subsequent deployment phases of IFMS. The IFMS system has expanded to include new users and interfaces specific to the various implementation groups through a mature and structured knowledge transfer process with the IFMS project. This has been vital to the integration of the IFMS system into HSE to date. This current Application Managed Service (AMS) contract is providing level 2, level 3 and level 4 support to the SAP Centre of Excellence (CoE) for all HSE Statutory sites and TUSLA, currently live on IFMS and this ongoing support is vital to the success of the continued roll out of IFMS to the voluntary organisations. Via active management of this contract by the SAP CoE team, HSE has also avoided, and will continue to avoid some significant time and material charges by the utilisation of the existing contract resource. Without this extension in place the following risks will result: • The IFMS system will become unstable bringing risk to the operations of the HSE, TUSLA and Voluntary Organisations, including processes such as; the ability to pay vendors, purchasing and the incoming supply of materials, management of materials in NDC and IM sites, income services, accounting and reporting. • Required system patching and future upgrades will not be supported. • The experience of 11,000 current users will be impacted as incident management and required system Service and Change Requests would be curtailed. • There would be an immediate risk to the continued rollout of stage 2 of the IFMS system as post-hypercare support could not be provided.

title-proc.eng: Riverine Community Park Project

description-proc.eng: The Riverine Community Park will consist of the creation of new community park infrastructure with multi-purpose community facilities and amenities at Lifford and Strabane. The project includes a 120m span cycle and pedestrian bridge across the River Foyle linking the park areas. The works at Lifford will include: • Construction of a single storey community resource building with a gross internal floor area approx. 305m² • Provision of a multi-functional outdoor space and external stage area to accommodate a variety of outdoor events; • Creation of play areas, walkways and cycleways and all associated drainage requirements. • Associated landscaping inclusive of the wetlands of the River Foyle • Amenity lighting • Provision of car parking and provisions for cycle parking • Site Security including estate style fencing, 2.4m high security fencing and lockable vehicle and pedestrian gates • Construction of an access road connecting with Lifford. • Provision of a new 10kV ESB Substation and diversion underground of existing MV (10kV/20kV) ESB overhead cables traversing the site; • Provision of a new wastewater pumping station for onward transfer of foul wastewater to the local network; • Works on the foreshore including construction of a cast in-situ concrete slipway, 5m wide and the provision fishing pods and a farm access track over the existing flood defence • Landowner Accommodation works and associated spectator stand building to accommodate 123 no. persons. The works at Strabane will include: • Access to Riverine Park via A5, including a new controlled pedestrian crossing point. • Access to the proposed Riverine Bridge via the existing Strabane North Greenway. • Associated landscaping and lighting works. The scheme also includes a 120m total span cycle and pedestrian bridge (with 90m and 30m spans) across the River Foyle. The Bridge will be a Design & Build element, with detailed design to be provided by the Contractor’s Team. The Contractor will be required to provide the following design / consultancy service within their team. • Bridge Designer • Archaeologist • Ecology consultant, including Ecological Clerk of Works.

title-proc.eng: 10009293-Development of inclusive financial services and products

description-proc.eng: Iraq faces a persistent gap between its people and the financial system. Banks have long leaned on large state-owned institutions, credit has flowed mainly to established borrowers, and micro and small businesses along with women entrepreneurs and displaced communities have been largely left out. ProDIGI project, full name Promoting Employment in the Digital and Green Economy in Iraq, is trying to change that in a practical, grounded way. ProDIGI is a multi-donor initiative commissioned by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), co-financed by the European Union, and implemented by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH. The project covers central and southern Iraq as well as the Kurdistan Region, with a focus on areas where joblessness, displacement, and limited access to services overlap. Within the project, Output 3 targets the financial inclusion side of the challenge. The starting point is a clear-eyed look at what the sector lacks: financial service providers that are capable, willing, and equipped to design products that fit the people they are supposed to serve. Banks and microfinance institutions in Iraq today mostly offer standardised products with high collateral requirements and limited digital capabilities. Reaching women led small businesses, rural communities, or young entrepreneurs running green or tech ventures requires a different kind of product, and often a different kind of institution. To bridge that gap, the project works directly with Iraqi financial service providers: banks, microfinance institutions, digital payment companies, fintechs, and government lending programmes. The approach combines needs assessments, hands-on advisory services, staff training, product design support, and pilot testing. The goal is not to deliver a finished product from outside, but to build the knowledge and process capacity within each institution so that change remains after the project ends. By the close of the assignment, at least three new or significantly adapted financial products must be in place, and these products must be actively reaching real users at a minimum of 950 individuals and 50 companies. The work also emphasises gender equality: women-led businesses are a priority target group, and all capacity-building activities must include a meaningful share of women participants. The broader context matters too. Iraq's Central Bank launched the national financial inclusion strategy that encourages digital payments, SME lending, and consumer protection improvements. ProDIGI project aligns directly with those priorities, making it both a practical intervention at the level of individual institutions and a contribution to the country's wider financial sector development. The selected firm will work directly with three to five financial service providers (FSPs) operating in Iraq. These may include commercial banks, microfinance institutions, digital payment providers, fintechs, and government lending schemes. GIZ will have pre-selected up to two FSPs before the contract starts, so work can begin without delay. The remaining FSPs will be selected by the contractor and GIZ jointly, based on agreed criteria.

description-proc.eng: Invitation to a supplier conference for the Norwegian Defence ́s digital transformation in Fanehallen 5 October 2026 The Norwegian Defence and Defence Material Agency invites tenderers, research and education institutions as well as other relevant actors to a supplier conference 5 October 2015 at 09.00-12.00 in Fanehallen at Akershus fortress. The Norwegian Armed Forces are facing a historic commitment to digitalisation and technological modernisation. The aim is to strengthen the Norwegian Defence ́s operative ability through a modern digital foundation, increased use of data and artificial intelligence, stronger interaction across the branches of the armed forces and better decision support in all domains. In the coming years, significant investments will be made including modernisation of the Norwegian Armed Forces' secure platforms, the development of the future digital work surface, modernisation of performance critical joint systems (ERP), establishment and modernisation of data centre, network and communication capacity, strengthened cyber security, utilisation of artificial intelligence as well as the establishment of modern platform and cloud services. The Norwegian Armed Forces cannot realise and succeed with this ambition alone. The Norwegian Armed Forces: The sector's need for digital capabilities and the effect Road ahead for digital capabilities: Strategic commitments, priorities, future needs and desired effects for the sector's digital development.      Norwegian Defence Materiel Agency: Procurements and market dialogue Strategies for procurement and market involvement in order to realise the future of digital defence. The conference is a part of the Norwegian Defence ́s market dialogue and is being held to increase mutual understanding between the defence sector and the market. The information presented shall contribute to better predictability for suppliers and form the basis for future procurements and collaboration possibilities. Participation in the conference does not provide any competitive advantage in later procurements. Any future procurements will be made in accordance with the procurement regulations and announced in the ordinary way. Register via the link below: The supplier conference 5 October 2026 Registration deadline is 1 October, 15:00. Due to capacity and security reasons, there can be limits on the number of participants. Each company is invited to provide up to two representatives if the company has fewer than 200 employees, three representatives of 200-400 employees and four representatives if the company has more than 400 employees. There will be access and ID control by the entrance. The strategic management documents will be digitally made available right after the conference. title-proc.eng: 10021316-Lot 1: Strengthening MSME Competitiveness, Market Access and Business Environment Reform in Benin

description-proc.eng: Benin's economy has experienced strong growth in recent years, with GDP growth estimated at around 6-7% annually. Nevertheless, this growth has not translated sufficiently into sustainable employment and income opportunities for the majority of the population. Micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), which represent more than 95% of registered businesses in Benin, continue to face major structural constraints limiting their competitiveness, productivity and job creation potential. These constraints include limited access to finance and markets, low levels of innovation and digitalisation, weak managerial and technical capacities, insufficient quality infrastructure, and a mismatch between labour market needs and available skills. The project "Employment-oriented promotion of the competitiveness of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises" (ProPME 2) aims to improve the competitiveness of MSMEs in selected sectors and regions in Benin with a strong employment impact. The project focuses particularly on enterprises operating in the agri-food sector, renewable energies, crafts and services, as well as on strengthening entrepreneurial ecosystems and labour market intermediation structures. Particular attention is given to women-led enterprises and young entrepreneurs. The project contributes to Benin"s National Development Plan 2018-2025, the national SME promotion strategy and the national employment promotion strategy. It is implemented as part of the wider programme "Improvement of income and employment situation in Benin", jointly supported by German Development Cooperation through GIZ and KfW. In addition, the project supports the implementation of the Alliance for Product Quality in Africa (AfPQ), a multi-actor initiative implemented by GIZ and PTB to improve product quality and market access under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). The module is structured around three main outputs: - Output 1 aims to strengthen the entrepreneurial, technical and market integration capacities of MSMEs through tailored training, coaching and quality management support. - Output 2 aims to improve the business environment and strengthen support institutions involved in MSME development, quality infrastructure and public-private dialogue. - Output 3 aims to improve labour market intermediation and the alignment between vocational training and the skills needs of MSMEs.

description-proc.eng: Benin's economy is experiencing sustained economic growth, with real GDP growth estimated at around 6.4 % in 2023 and projected to remain above 6 % over the coming years. However, this growth has not translated into sufficient decent employment opportunities for the majority of the population. Micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), which represent more than 95 % of registered enterprises, continue to face structural constraints including low productivity, weak integration into markets and value chains, limited access to finance and skilled labour, insufficient digitalisation, and inadequate business support services. Women-led enterprises and enterprises located in northern regions are particularly affected by these challenges. The Government of Benin has adopted several national strategies to strengthen economic productivity, employment promotion and SME competitiveness, including the National Development Plan 2018-2025, the national SME promotion strategy, the national employment policy and the "Benin Alafia 2060" vision. In parallel, the country aims to strengthen labour market governance through improved labour market information systems and territorial employment promotion approaches. The Federal Republic of Germany supports Benin in the implementation of these reforms through, among others, the project "Employment-oriented promotion of the competitiveness of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises" (ProPME 2). The project aims to improve the competitiveness of MSMEs in selected sectors and regions with a positive impact on employment. It focuses on the food processing industry, renewable energies, crafts and services sectors, as well as employment promotion and labour market intermediation. The module is structured around three main outputs: Output 1 aims to strengthen the competitiveness and growth capacities of MSMEs through tailored support, coaching and training measures. Output 2 aims to improve framework conditions for MSMEs through strengthened cooperation mechanisms, institutional support and public-private dialogue. Output 3 aims to improve the conditions for the placement of qualified workers in MSMEs through strengthened employment governance, labour market intermediation and labour market information systems.

description-proc.fra: L'Institut de géochimie et de pétrologie de l'ETH Zurich souhaite remplacer son microscope électronique à balayage (MEB) analytique actuel par un nouvel appareil équipé d'une source à émission de champ, de détecteurs d'électrons secondaires (SE) et d'électrons rétrodiffusés (BSE) de haute performance, ainsi que d'un spectromètre à dispersion d'énergie (EDS) de pointe à grande surface (≥ 100 mm²). Parmi les options possibles, nous sommes intéressés par des offres incluant un détecteur de cathodoluminescence panchromatique et/ou monochromatique d'entrée de gamme. L'objectif principal de cet instrument sera de réaliser des analyses quantitatives précises et exactes par EDS, en s'appuyant sur un protocole de quantification rigoureux incluant l'utilisation de matériaux de référence et une correction de matrice complète (ZAF, phi-rho-z ou équivalent). L'instrument devra disposer d'une chambre de grande taille permettant d'accueillir simultanément au moins 3 lames minces pétrographiques et 6 supports circulaires en résine époxy (format 1 pouce). Il devra également être programmable afin de permettre l'exécution de séries d'analyses quantitatives EDS automatisées d'une durée supérieure à 24 heures. Pour plus de détails, voir le cahier des charges.
description-proc.deu: Das Institut für Geochemie und Petrologie der ETH Zürich beabsichtigt, sein bestehendes analytisches Rasterelektronenmikroskop (REM) durch ein neues System zu ersetzen. Dieses soll mit einer Feldemissionsquelle, SE- und leistungsstarken BSE-Detektoren sowie einem hochmodernen energiedispersiven Röntgenspektrometer (EDS) mit grossem Detektorbereich (≥ 100 mm²) ausgestattet sein. Wir sind zudem an Angeboten für einen panchromatischen und/oder einen monochromatischen Kathodolumineszenz-Detektor (Einstiegsmodell) interessiert. Hauptziel des Instruments ist die Durchführung präziser und genauer quantitativer EDS-Analysen unter Anwendung eines strengen Quantifizierungsprotokolls, das die Verwendung von Referenzmaterialien sowie eine vollständige Matrixkorrektur (ZAF, phi-rho-z oder gleichwertig) umfasst. Das Gerät muss über eine grosse Probenkammer verfügen, die Platz für mindestens drei petrographische Dünnschliffe und sechs in Epoxidharz eingebettete Rundproben (Durchmesser 1 Zoll) bietet. Zudem soll das System programmierbar sein, um automatisierte quantitative EDS-Analysereihen mit einer Laufzeit von mehr als 24 Stunden zu ermöglichen. Details siehe Pflichtenheft.
description-proc.eng: The Institute of Geochemistry and Petrology at ETH Zürich is seeking to upgrade its existing analytical scanning electron microscope (SEM) for a new SEM equipped with a field emission gun, secondary electrons detector (SE) and high-performance backscattered electron detectors (BSE), and a state-of-the-art large area (≥ 100 mm2) energy dispersive spectrometer (EDS). Among several options, we welcome offers for panchromatic and/or entry-level monochromatic cathodoluminescence detector. The main goal of this instrument will be to provide precise and accurate quantitative analyses by EDS using a rigorous quantification protocol that includes the use of reference materials and a full matrix correction (ZAF, phi-rho-z, or equivalent). The instrument should have a large chamber to allow a minimum of 3 petrographic thin sections and 6 one-inch epoxy round mounts. It should be programmable so that we run series of >24 hours of automated quantitative EDS analyses. For further details, please refer to the specifications.

title-proc.eng: Plug’N’Teach quantum computer and training

description-proc.eng: The ConScience Plug’N’Teach quantum computer and its associated training offering are unique in the market because they combine, within a single integrated educational platform, superconducting quantum hardware, cryogenic infrastructure, quantum-control electronics, and an open system architecture specifically designed for teaching, evaluation, and hands on technology development. 1. Purpose-built superconducting quantum hardware The Qubit-in-a-Box 2 (QiB2) superconducting quantum chip is specifically designed for teaching, characterization, and evaluation of superconducting quantum devices. It incorporates both individual qubits and coupled qubit structures of different types, enabling experiments with progressively increasing levels of complexity. This makes the platform unique in the market and suitable for education ranging from bachelor’s and master’s courses to PhD-level training and research projects. Unlike systems primarily designed for remote quantum-computing access or narrowly defined research applications, the QiB2 provides direct experimental access to the underlying quantum hardware and its physical behavior. 2. Proven cryogenic infrastructure The system is based on dilution-refrigerator technology from Bluefors Oy, Finland, the leading supplier of cryogenic systems for superconducting quantum-computing applications. Bluefors has extensive experience in the installation and operation of dilution refrigerators in quantum research environments, providing a mature and reliable cryogenic foundation for both teaching and experimental work. 3. Integrated quantum-control platform The control electronics from Quantum Machines provide a native quantum-control environment purpose-built for quantum processors. The platform combines real-time orchestration with intuitive pulse-level programming, supporting both educational exploration and advanced research without requiring the customer to develop a custom control-hardware stack. This integrated approach is essential for maximizing the QiB2’s pedagogical value, enabling rapid iteration in university teaching and evaluation workflows, and establishing a robust foundation for future in-house hardware and software development. 4. Open architecture and comprehensive educational scope A key differentiator of the Plug’N’Teach system is its open architecture and the horizontal integration of leading component providers in superconducting quantum computing within a platform explicitly focused on education and workforce development. The system is designed not as a closed appliance, but as an environment in which students and researchers can access, understand, characterize, and modify multiple layers of the technology stack. Users are therefore able not only to operate a quantum computer, but also to study the interaction between quantum devices, cryogenic systems, control electronics, pulse sequences, calibration procedures, and software. They can develop their own hardware and software solutions and benchmark them against the reference configuration provided by the Plug’N’Teach system. This breadth is particularly important for quantum-workforce development. Building and operating quantum computers requires expertise extending well beyond PhD-level quantum physics and includes competencies in electrical engineering, microwave engineering, cryogenics, control systems, software development, calibration, system integration, operation, and maintenance. For these reasons, the distinguishing feature of the ConScience Plug’N’Teach solution is not only the single components in isolation, but the availability of this specific combination of purpose-built superconducting quantum hardware, established cryogenic infrastructure, native quantum-control electronics, open system access, and structured educational support in one integrated platform. To the best of our knowledge, no other supplier currently offers an equivalent complete system with the same combination of capabilities and educational scope.

title-proc.eng: Project "FreeBSD – AI-Assisted Vulnerability Discovery"

description-proc.deu: Dieser Dienstleistungsvertrag betrifft das FOSS-Betriebssystem FreeBSD und umfasst die Erforschung, wie künstliche Intelligenz die Open-Source-Wartung stärken kann, wobei der Schwerpunkt auf dem Prozess des FreeBSD-Sicherheitsteams liegt, Schwachstellen zu finden, zu validieren, zu beheben und offenzulegen sowie Sicherheitshinweise zu erstellen. FreeBSD ist ein modernes, Unix-ähnliches Betriebssystem, das unter permissive license veröffentlicht wird. title-proc.eng: Provision of the design of a non-native and invasive species surveillance and monitoring programme for the island of Ireland

description-proc.eng: Surveillance and monitoring of invasive species in both Ireland and Northern Ireland is currently fragmented and not considered sufficient to meet the requirements of legal instruments and agreements. The National Biodiversity Data Centre in the Republic of Ireland and the Centre for Environmental Data and Recording (CEDaR) in Northern Ireland, are the two national record centres for biological data on the island of Ireland. While both receive and act as a repository for biological data, there are sources of information that are not routinely and/or timely reported to either organisation. In the case of the highest risk invasive non-native species, this creates undesirable and preventable barriers to understanding the distribution of invasive species across the island of Ireland, and in certain situations, delays response action when a species might be highly localised. This situation can impact on Ireland and Northern Ireland’s ability to effectively understand the true distribution of invasive species on the island of Ireland, with real world impacts on effective management and prevention measures. However, under the new Shared Island Biosecurity and Invasive Species Initiative, there is an opportunity to review current surveillance and monitoring programmes active in both jurisdictions and make recommendations on a new system that effectively and efficiently captures relevant data for Ireland and Northern Ireland.

title-proc.eng: Supply, Installation and maintenance of a PEM Electrolyser for Hydrogen Production at JRC Ispra

description-proc.eng: The procurement entails the design, manufacturing, delivery, installation, and commissioning of a Proton Exchange Membrane (PEM) electrolysis system for hydrogen production at the JRC Ispra site. The core of the system is a 50 Nm3/h electrolyser (which must be upgradable to 100 Nm3/h) that delivers hydrogen at an outlet pressure of 30 barg. The main equipment will be delivered in a containerized/skid version divided into three specific areas: a control panel area with the AC/DC converter, a water purification unit, and an ATEX­classified area containing the stacks and gas purification treatment. In addition to the containerized unit, the scope of supply includes several external components: ­ An MV/LV transformer ­ A thermal management system (dry cooler) ­ A low­pressure hydrogen storage system consisting of a cylinder rack at 30 bar with a total volume of 5 m3 ­ A gas blender installed on the outlet piping after the storage Finally, the procurement includes a comprehensive service package covering the Factory Acceptance Test (FAT), Site Acceptance Test (SAT), ATEX verification, staff training, two years of spare parts, and a 3­year maintenance contract. Reason for Purchasing The primary objective of this procurement is to produce green hydrogen by harnessing the renewable energy generated from the JRC Ispra site's internal photovoltaic (PV) plant. Currently, the site has a 1.35 MWp PV installation, which is planned to be expanded to 2 MWp and eventually 3 MWp in the future. Instead of using battery systems, the JRC intends to use the excess energy from this PV plant to power the electrolyser for self­consumption. The hydrogen produced will then be blended into the natural gas pipeline (up to a 10% volume blend) to feed the site's co­generators. A dedicated technical sizing analysis concluded that a modular 2x250 kW electrolyser is the optimal choice, as it offers the best compromise between the available PV power, the number of operating hours, and the demand from the co­generators across current and future PV expansion scenarios
